messages:
Anya Patel: Heads-up — I ran a 2k-sample calibration sweep on redwood-medium-v2 with the new FP8 kernels and Im seeing a weird perf/quality tradeoff. P50 latency up ~12% on streaming paths, throughput down ~18% for small-batch (<8) workloads.
Mike Chen: Can you paste the profiler output? nvprof/nsys or our microbench harness output is ideal. :thinking:
Anya Patel: Microbench output below. Its from the nightly perf runner: 
```
model: redwood-medium-v2
config: fp8-perchannel + mixed-quant gating
batch=4, seq=128
old (int8-fused): p50=42.7ms, throughput=23.5 req/s
new (fp8-fused): p50=47.9ms, throughput=19.3 req/s
kernel-switch overhead: ~2.8ms per request (KV miss)
KV warmup hitrate: 82%
calib-dataset: sampled web/QA mix (n=2000)
observed outliers: 0.6% of activations > 4 sigma
```
Rachel Solis: Interesting — the kernel-switch overhead + KV miss pattern smells like ABI/packing inefficiency when kernels change precision mid-seq. Did you see an increase in memcpy or launch overhead on the timeline?
Anya Patel: Yes, timeline shows frequent small kernel launches. When per-channel calibration produced a few extreme scales, we auto-switched to a fallback kernel (per-tensor) for those layers which forced the runtime to use a different fused path -> extra copies.
Sebastian Gomez: That jives. Mixed-precision gating that picks different execution graphs per-layer will break continuous batching: it fragments the batch groups and disables some kernel fusion heuristics.
Mike Chen: Is the regression repeatable if you clip outliers in the calib set? E.g., replace >3 sigma activations with clipped values and rerun quantize/pack.
Anya Patel: I tried clipping to 3 sigma in-place — quality (accuracy on eval set) stayed within 0.2% but perf improved: p50 down to 44.1ms, throughput 21.1 req/s. So clipping helps but the change feels heuristic-y.
Rachel Solis: That suggests our calibration dataset has heavy tails. If outliers are causing per-channel scales to explode, per-channel quantization will force fallbacks for only a tiny subset of channels but still kill fusion.
Sebastian Gomez: Proposal: change gating to be layer-aware instead of channel-aware for live routing. Compute a per-layer SNR metric from calib stats. If layer-SNR < threshold, force per-tensor quant path for the whole layer at compile time and avoid mid-batch switching. That reduces graph variance.
Mike Chen: Agree. We should also make the runtime treat tiny-fraction channel fallbacks as clipped exceptions rather than whole-layer fallbacks by default — or perform a cheap remap that keeps the fused kernel.
Anya Patel: We prototyped a "gatewalk" policy: evaluate per-channel ratio of scale to median-scale, mark channels >K as "tail"; if tail_count < T_percent, apply channel-clamp (clip/scatter) and keep per-channel kernels. If tail_count >= T_percent, switch whole-layer to per-tensor. 
Anya Patel: With gatewalk (K=4, T=2%), results: p50=43.2ms, throughput=22.4 req/s, accuracy delta +0.03%. Looks promising.
Rachel Solis: Nice. How sensitive to K/T are you? Need to make defaults robust across models.
Anya Patel: K sweep shows knee around 3.5-4.5. T around 1-3% stabilizes perf/quality. But some safety-net models with very long tails need stricter T.
Mike Chen: Ops question: does gatewalk increase profiling cost? We currently run one calibration pass. Gatewalk needs channel histograms + tail counts, so same pass but extra aggregation — cheap.
Sebastian Gomez: Another operational thing: the batching heuristics need a small enhancement to avoid splitting batches when layer execution graph differs. If the runtime can tag requests with layer-graph-hash and batch only compatible ones, fusion remains intact. That will add complexity to the grouping but could eliminate the copy/launch overhead.
Anya Patel: True — maybe a two-tier batcher: prefer native fusion groups but allow fallback batches for incompatible ones. That reduces tail impact on p50.
Mike Chen: Sounds like a plan. Can you open a perf repro with the saved microbench config + the gatewalk patch? Put nsys flame + timeline trace in the ticket. Ill try a larger model (redwood-large-v1) to validate scale effects.
Anya Patel: Will do. Ill also add a quick eval harness measuring token-accuracy on the calibration holdout set (2% held for tail detection).
Rachel Solis: One last note — document the default behavior: per-tensor fallback should be global-layer, not per-request. Avoid dynamic kernel swaps mid-request unless explicitly allowed by opt-in flag.
Sebastian Gomez: +1. Keep dynamic kernel swapping behind an opt-in runtime flag until we nail the batching and gatewalk heuristics.
